unmapped.14: check-ci gate not green: shown by the check-ci edges
unmapped.20: PR title fails the conventional-commit gate: operational

unmapped.1: handover root or GO key unreadable: operational
unmapped.2: usage or anchor handoff refusal: operational
unmapped.5: trust-reviewed id has no GO verdict: operational
unmapped.6: fork adapter refusal: out of scope
unmapped.7: fork adapter PR state refusal: out of scope

unmapped.telegram: operator inbound message: not a workflow decision
unmapped.tick: generic action-key change: shown as the tick node
unmapped.board-stale: board housekeeping: operational, immediate in zero-batching mode
unmapped.housekeeping: due digest of buffered board, status-sweep and informational marker changes: operational
unmapped.orphan-pr: an open PR with no live worker record or queue: hold: the chief relaunches or names it, operational triage
unmapped.unwatched: a live worker missing from the fleet manifest: watch housekeeping, not a workflow decision
unmapped.doctor: a new doctor WARN/FAIL check id: the chief fixes, tickets or rules on it, operational triage
unmapped.pool-stale: a pool disposition whose blocker shipped: the chief re-rules the parked ticket, operational triage
unmapped.focus: FOCUS page refresh failure or stale dirty state: operational
unmapped.status-sweep: Jira status sweep moved or missed tickets: operational
unmapped.resolve: a worker's BLOCKED resolve marker: the chief resolves the thread itself, not a workflow decision

unmapped.BLOCKED: worker status: escalation to the chief, no graph decision
unmapped.HALTED: worker status: stop, no graph decision
unmapped.PARKED-USAGE: worker status: usage park, no graph decision
unmapped.RESUMED: worker status: resume, no graph decision

unmapped.ERROR: config error, missing ci:go label or failed label write: operational, the next event retries
unmapped.ALERT: a hard reviewer is unavailable: an alert printed beside its HOLD, not a separate transition
unmapped.MANUAL-RELEASE: a ci:go set by hand: reported once, the heavy run has already started
unmapped.PENDING-RELEASE: the read-only preview ready-check.sh prints: writes nothing

stages.name: Start
stages.purpose: where does a ticket come from, how hard was its idea tested, and what did that cost? It is for you, deciding which ideas need a grill or a spec first. Most go straight to a ticket.

line.back: the grill changed it: think again

gates: The ticket checker: it refuses a Task, Story or Bug that is missing a section.
The signed-spec gate for a core ticket: planned for this version.
DoD and Proof are checked again when the chief picks the ticket, in phase 3.
back: A section is empty: the draft is parked until it is filled (a count, not a 7-day number).
The grill changed the idea: back to step 1.
A critic finds a hole in the spec: the spec is redone.
stages.noSource: Nothing records when an idea arrives, and the chief's planning cost is pooled, not counted per ticket.

stages.name: Plan and design
stages.purpose: is this ticket planned and sized, and is a page change designed and approved before anyone builds it? It is for you, approving designs. Every ticket gets a plan; most skip the design.
gates: The plan critic: a core ticket's plan is checked, and signed with its spec planned for this version.
The design-approval gate: planned for the next version. Not live.
The estimate is advisory: it never changes the start.
back: A critic finds a hole in the plan: the plan is redone.
Changes asked on the design: it is redrawn.
stages.noSource: Nothing records an estimate or a design approval yet.

stages.name: Assign
stages.purpose: how does the chief turn tickets into running workers, and what holds a ticket back? It is for you, when a ticket is not starting.
gates: DoD and Proof when picked: a ticket without them is dropped. This is printed, not recorded.
The collision check: one writer per file.
A dependency chain: a ticket blocked by an open one waits.
Hold labels: waiting for you, design put off, held.
Start checks: the fleet cap, usage, a refusal page waiting for you.
This version: a core ticket needs a signed spec before its brief.
back: Start refused: the chief waits for a free slot, or asks for your decision.
No DoD or Proof: back to filling the ticket.
An AFK shift is a second way in: it fans tickets out as helper sessions, each in its own worktree. This page draws only the chief's path.
stages.noSource: Dropped tickets and refused starts are printed, not recorded.

stages.name: Build
stages.purpose: what does a worker do before anyone reviews the change, and which checks run on each commit and push? It is for you, reading a worker's progress.

line.gate: a review is owed before the PR

gates: The commit message check.
The checks on every push.
A push that needs a review goes through and leaves a review-owed marker; the PR cannot open until the review runs.
back: A commit refused by the message check: not recorded.
The Build time includes the automated review rounds of phase 5, which run before the PR opens.

stages.name: Review
stages.purpose: how many review rounds does a change take, and what ends them? It is for you, when a PR seems stuck in review.
gates: The round limit: 3 rounds, then one extra round on what changed.
CodeRabbit.
The required reviewers.
back: A finding is agreed: fix it, push, and start a new round (3 rounds, then the limit).
At the round limit, the chief grants one more round.

stages.name: Check and approve
stages.purpose: what must be true before a change may merge, who approves it, and where does it go back? It is for you, when a change is green but not merged.
gates: ci:go: planned for this version. Today it is switched off (step 30).
CI: every required check.
The readiness check.
The judge, only on a trust path.
back: The readiness check fails: back to READY. not counted
The judge says NO-GO: back to a fix. not counted
CI is red and the PR is at fault: fix it and start a new round.

stages.name: Merge and wrap up
stages.purpose: what happens after the merge, and how does the chief close the work out? It is for you, checking that nothing was left behind.
gates: The merge guard on a merge typed by hand.
The merge waits for green CI and a GO.
back: A merge is refused (no GO, a trust path, or a red main): not recorded.
The chief files leftover work as follow-ups, which start again at phase 1.
